classification.analysis: Labour collapsed from 33.7% (2024 election) to 18.7% in polling, overtaken by Reform UK at 26.9%. Historic May 2026 local election losses triggered internal party calls for Starmer's resignation. Economic malaise and far-right surge define a government in crisis barely two years into office.

Merz government faces historic collapse just 13 months in. AfD overtakes coalition in polls for first time. Chancellor's 15% approval is lowest ever recorded. Consumer confidence plunged in May amid energy crisis fears and Iran conflict spillover. Coalition infighting mirrors previous government failures. Five state elections in 2026 threaten further AfD gains, especially in eastern states where party polls near 40%.

Macron faces catastrophic collapse with record-low 18% approval. Rassemblement National dominates at 35% as cordon sanitaire crumbles. May Day saw massive protests against austerity while PM Lecornu barely survived no-confidence votes. Consumer confidence hit three-year low amid Iran war fallout. Far-right positioned to win 2027 presidency as political establishment disintegrates.

Sánchez faces cascading corruption scandals: his wife indicted for influence peddling, brother on trial, Socialist Party headquarters raided May 2026. Thousands marched demanding resignation May 23. Coalition polling 10 points below 2023 election. Former PM Zapatero under investigation. Opposition PP leads comfortably while Vox consolidates third position at 17.6%.

Following Denmark's March 2026 election delivering the Social Democrats their worst result since 1903, Frederiksen remains caretaker PM after two months of failed coalition talks. Centre-right negotiations collapsed in May, returning mandate to Frederiksen. Consumer confidence plunged to -18.6 in April while the far-right Danish People's Party surged from 2.6% to 11.1%, quadrupling support amid fragmentation across twelve parliamentary parties.

One Nation overtook Labor in May 2026 polling for the first time, reaching 28-31% after the government's unpopular property tax budget. Albanese holds a net -20% approval rating. Labor won a landslide reelection just one year ago with 34.7%, but has collapsed to 26-28% as One Nation surges from 6.2%.

Martin's coalition has dropped 9 points since the 2024 election, trailing Sinn Féin by 10+ points. Fuel protests in April sparked internal party criticism and questions about his leadership. Consumer confidence remains depressed despite slight May recovery. Housing crisis and cost-of-living pressures dominate discourse as Ireland prepares for EU Council presidency.

Jetten's three-month-old centrist coalition faces headwinds from plummeting consumer confidence and unpopular austerity (pension age hikes, benefit cuts), yet D66 gained seats in March municipal elections. PVV has collapsed from 24.7% (2023) to 13% now, firmly contained. Coalition polls 52% versus 57% at election—modest erosion but stable governance. Far-right remains fragmented and excluded.

Montenegro's minority coalition has plunged from 32% to 25% in polls while Chega consolidates at 22% as second force. Government backed Chega-supported migration crackdown expelling 18,000 people and pursues constitutional reform with far-right votes. Storm Kristin disaster response and Iran war fallout deepen crisis as consumer confidence hits two-year low and Socialist president enters cohabitation.

Støre's Labour government faces a dramatic polling collapse just eight months after re-election victory. Progress Party now leads by 8 points, reversing September's result. Despite improving consumer confidence and securing the landmark Narvik defense pact with France on May 27, Labour has shed 6 points while the far-right surges. Economic improvements haven't translated to political support.

Takaichi's far-right-aligned LDP government secured historic supermajority in February, absorbing Sanseito's anti-immigrant agenda. Recent smear campaign scandal and persistent local election defeats reveal authoritarian drift beneath high national approval. Consumer confidence declining from February peak as economic anxieties mount.

Michal's Reform-Eesti 200 coalition has collapsed to a record-low 14.1% from 44.5% at the 2023 election. Parliament approved a supplementary budget with deficit rising to 4.3% of GDP driven by defense spending. EKRE has slightly declined to 13.5% while conservative Isamaa leads opposition at 26.3%. Nuclear energy debate and cyberattack concerns dominate recent discourse.

Coalition collapsed to 25% from 29% in 2022, losing parliamentary majority. Sweden Democrats negotiated March agreement for cabinet positions, ending cordon sanitaire. Consumer confidence hit lowest level since August 2025. Ukraine fighter jet deal announced late May as September election approaches with far-right poised to enter government directly.

Orpo's coalition faces mounting pressure as support collapses to 38% from 48% at election, losing parliamentary majority. May drone scare exposed preparedness gaps, prompting emergency household safety guides. Consumer confidence hit -8.7, worst since February 2025, amid 9.5% unemployment and continued austerity. Finns Party polling halved to 13.6% as economic malaise deepens.

Mitsotakis governs with majority but faces 11-point polling decline since 2023 amid Tempi rail disaster aftermath, OPEKEPE farm-subsidy scandal, and persistent inflation. Alexis Tsipras launched new ELAS party May 27, fragmenting opposition into political 'Babel'. Greek Solution remains marginal at 5.6%. New Democracy entered pre-election mode targeting 2027, banking on opposition disarray and stability narrative despite consumer confidence below historical average.

Stocker's three-party coalition has collapsed from 56.5% at the 2024 election to just 45.7% now, with their majority on a knife-edge. FPÖ dominates at 37%, up from 28.8%. In late May, Stocker adopted hardline rhetoric on deportations and ECHR reinterpretation, mimicking far-right positions. The coalition passed EU migration laws over FPÖ opposition, but voter flight continues unabated.

De Wever's Arizona coalition polls at 57.3%, up from 49.8% at election, maintaining comfortable majority. Vlaams Belang rises modestly to 16% but remains contained below coalition partners. Government enacted labor market reforms and austerity measures for defense spending. De Wever made headlines warning Europe against U.S. dependence at Davos and controversially suggesting normalizing Russia ties amid Iranian conflict.

Luxon survived a confidence vote in April as National dropped to 30%, down from 39% at election. NZ First has surged above 6%, eating National's lunch and causing coalition tensions. Consumer confidence crashed from 107 in January to 80 in April amid Middle East crisis before modest May recovery. Coalition clings to razor-thin polling lead six months before the November election.

Meloni's far-right government faces mounting pressure after March's judicial reform referendum defeat shattered her invincibility. Coalition polls show loss of parliamentary majority. Recent weeks saw aggressive EU confrontation over fiscal flexibility for energy costs, with Meloni attacking Brussels as a bureaucratic behemoth. Government slashed growth outlook to 0.6% amid energy crisis. Consumer confidence down 3 points year-over-year. Local elections this week test resilience ahead of 2027 national vote.

Babiš's coalition with far-right SPD has sparked mass protests over media independence plans and renewed scrutiny of Agrofert conflicts. Coalition polling has dropped 6 points since October 2025 election. Consumer confidence declining amid media freedom concerns and persistent corruption allegations in first six months.

Trump's approval collapsed to 37% by May 2026 from 47% at inauguration, driven by tariff-induced inflation and economic anxiety. Independent approval at 34% has entered wave-election territory. Weekend military strikes with Iran continue as ceasefire negotiations stall, with gas prices elevated and consumer confidence on prices hitting record lows of -47.

Magyar secured landmark EU funds breakthrough worth €16.4 billion in Brussels talks with von der Leyen this week. Consumer confidence posted unprecedented 16-point monthly surge after his May 9 inauguration. Parliament reversed ICC withdrawal, signaling institutional reset. President Sulyok defied resignation demand, creating minor early friction, but polling shows Tisza support surging to 68%.

Fico's coalition has collapsed from 43% to 29% in polls while dismantling anti-corruption bodies and pursuing pro-Russian policy. His May 9 Moscow visit made him the EU's sole attending leader. Consumer confidence hit a three-year low. Republika's 11% represents opposition far-right, but SNS—already in government—provides nationalist governance.

Milei's approval plunged to 36% amid corruption scandals involving Chief of Staff Adorni and wage declines of 9% since taking office. Mass protests erupted May 12 as economic pain intensifies despite Fitch's B- upgrade. Opposition remains fragmented, with far-left Bregman now Argentina's most popular politician, not Peronist leaders.

Netanyahu's coalition collapsed in May 2026 after ultra-Orthodox partners withdrew support over military conscription exemptions. Parliament voted 110-0 to dissolve, triggering early elections likely in September. Coalition polling has crashed from 64 seats in 2022 to just 56 now, losing its majority. Netanyahu vowed to seize 70% of Gaza despite ceasefire terms while facing corruption trials and 75%+ disapproval.

Police violently raided opposition CHP headquarters in late May 2026 after courts nullified leader Özel's election. Istanbul Mayor İmamoğlu, Erdoğan's main rival, was arrested in March on 140+ charges. Systematic crackdown on opposition intensifies as inflation persists near 60% and consumer confidence remains deeply pessimistic.

Tusk's coalition crumbles as junior partners poll below threshold while far-right Confederation and KKP surge to combined 25%. Presidential vetoes block reforms. Combined right-wing forces poll at 51%, positioning for 2027 takeover. US troop withdrawal and Nawrocki's constitutional gambit deepen crisis. Coalition would lose majority on current numbers.

Carney maintains strong 44% polling fourteen months after dramatic election victory driven by Trump threats. Liberals secured majority via four Conservative floor-crossings in April 2026. However, economy shed 110,000 jobs since late 2025 and consumer confidence declining. Pressure mounting to deliver on infrastructure, defense spending, and economic diversification promises. PPC remains negligible at 1%.

Lee marks first year with 64% approval, second-highest since democratization. Stock market surged 90% under his presidency, fueling economic optimism. However, June 3 local elections have become a referendum on his administration, marking his first major political test beyond the initial honeymoon period.

Sheinbaum faces mounting corruption concerns after US indicted Sinaloa governor for cartel ties. On May 31, she accused Washington of political interference, claiming destabilization efforts intensified since April CIA agent deaths. Approval declined 14 points from inauguration but remains majority. Consumer confidence remains in pessimistic territory below 50 threshold.
